etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French national, corresponding to nation +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: Pertaining to a nation or country, especially as a whole; affecting, shared by, or existing throughout all of a nation. [from 16th c.]
Belonging to or characteristic of a specific nation or country, as opposed to others. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1791, James Boswell, Life of Johnson, Oxford, published 2008, page 599:
quote.text: ‘Come, come, don't deny it: they are really national. Why, now, the Adams are as liberal-minded men as any in the world: but, I don't know how it is, all their workmen are Scotch.’

definitions.definition: (usually in the plural) A tournament in which participants from all over the nation compete.
(usually in the plural, journalism) A national newspaper.

quote.citation: 1978, “Blondes (Have More Fun)”, performed by Rod Stewart:
quote.text: I had a crush on Bardot / Fell in love with Monroe / Read about 'em in the nationals / All the juicy little scandals
